This is because the model consumes the previous token, reads model weights, performs matrix-vector operations, updates attention state, samples the next token, and streams it back to the user. On a CPU-only node, the arithmetic units may be capable of more operations per second than the memory subsystem can feed when the batch size is small. This means the model can become memory-bandwidth bound: the time per output token is dominated by moving weights and intermediate data rather than by floating-point arithmetic alone.
